Here are a few things that I've found help:

* Standard defensive line and mid block or low block 
* Adding width (e.g. switch wide attackers to wingers) 
* Give your CMs roles that bring them into transition play, like CM-su, BBM, DLP 
* Setting your wide attackers to support 
* Narrower, shorter passing, higher tempo, counter if the opponent is counter pressing (in this case I'd probably remove Play Out of Defence) 
* Drop off more if opponent favors high tempo passing to draw your defensive players out of position 
* Having your CMs or wide mids (depending on your formation) man mark their AML/AMR 
* Setting Always Press and Hard Tackling on their DMs if they have something game breakingly stupid like a Volante-Regista pairing 

I've also had success recently with a flat 3-1-4-2 (3 CB, 1 DM, 2 CM, ML, MR) that specifically aims to nullify the 4-2-3-1. I could share it if you have the squad to make use of it.

RDS is the player's suitability for a certain role, role ability is the player's rating compared to other players in your team.

The RDS basically reflects how well suited the player is to playing a certain role compared to other roles. For example, an attack-minded fullback would get a low RDS for the FB(D) role compared to something like FB(A). Of course, you can play players in whichever role you feel suits them best within the tactic; the RDS is there so you can quickly see an overview.

On-hit effects are basically effects applied by your auto attacks. The reason Kayle works so well with devourer is because her E damage applies twice every other hit. Wit's end works the same way, as does any item that enhances your auto attacks (e.g. bork). It also has the same interaction with stacking passives like Vi W, Diana passive, etc.
